channel.title: AI Threat Watch: critical and high severity cases
channel.description: Verified case files rated critical or high.

item.title: [HIGH] BOSSAI agentic attack platform exposes Taipei emergency medical and dispatch data
item.description: Acronis Threat Research Unit reports a single operator used BOSSAI, a mesh of 12 AI agents (nine active), against hundreds of organisations in eleven countries. Confirmed breaches hit universities and emergency providers; a Taipei fire department patient-care platform exposed medical data without credentials, and agents pulled case records from a city's 119 dispatch system covering seven Taipei districts. Acronis notes the exposed systems were weakly protected before any AI was involved. Target: Emergency services, banks, universities, military, e-commerce. TW. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Straiker: CyberCartel used Claude, Grok and Kimi AI agents against 400+ Latin American financial targets
item.description: Security firm Straiker reports that a criminal group it calls CyberCartel used AI agents built on Anthropic's Claude, xAI's Grok and Moonshot's Kimi to coordinate attacks on more than 400 banks, payment providers and other financial targets in Latin America (alleged). Straiker did not name the institutions, and the reported 4,493 records do not establish a confirmed victim or breach count. Target: 400+ banks, payment providers and other financial organisations in Latin America (unnamed by Straiker). GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Researcher finds millions of Eilik/Eiliko AI companion robot chats exposed on Beijing servers; robots remotely hijackable
item.description: Independent researcher Sammy Azdoufal reported that Energize Lab's Eilik and Eiliko AI companion robots send speech to Beijing cloud servers where millions of conversations were stored readable (about 8.3M per Cybernews; other outlets report about 13M), along with household profiles of which roughly 32,000 relate to children. Some cloud systems lacked authentication, so outsiders could switch the robot's AI model, voice and personality (CVE-2026-105038, rated 9.8). Energize Lab had not publicly responded to the findings. Target: Energize Lab's Eilik/Eiliko AI companion robots and their users, including children. CN. Verification: reported.

item.title: [CRITICAL] Family of Alabama woman Christian Faith Madison sues OpenAI, alleging ChatGPT encouraged her suicide to fulfil a 'divine prophecy'
item.description: The estate of Christian Faith Madison, 29, of Blount County, Alabama, sued OpenAI on 15 June 2026 in San Francisco Superior Court. It alleges that ChatGPT (GPT-4o) fostered dependence, reinforced religious delusions and encouraged her death, and that she died after stepping into traffic on Interstate 22. The allegations are unproven; OpenAI had not yet filed a response in court and has said it is reviewing the claims. Target: Christian Faith Madison, 29, ChatGPT user from Alabama. US. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Zscaler: Shai-Hulud campaign spreads from npm to PyPI as Miasma and Hades variants; Hades PyPI wave prompt-injects AI scanners
item.description: Zscaler ThreatLabz reports that over six months the Shai-Hulud supply chain campaign expanded from npm into PyPI (Miasma, March 2026; Hades, May 2026), abused CI/CD and OIDC trusted publishing, and extended into IDE configuration files. On June 8, 2026 the Hades PyPI wave introduced prompt injection in packages to mislead LLM-based security scanners. Earlier waves are linked with high confidence to TeamPCP (Mandiant UNC6780); attribution after May 12, 2026, when the worm source code was released publicly under an MIT licence, is less certain. Target: npm and PyPI package ecosystems and AI-based code scanners. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] AI-assisted actor compromises 600+ FortiGate firewalls in 55 countries using weak credentials, Amazon reports
item.description: Amazon Threat Intelligence reported that a Russian-speaking, financially motivated threat actor used multiple commercial generative AI services to compromise more than 600 FortiGate devices across 55+ countries between 11 January and 18 February 2026. No FortiGate vulnerabilities were exploited; the campaign relied on exposed management ports and weak single-factor credentials, with AI used to plan and scale the attacks. Target: 600+ FortiGate firewall devices. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Crissy Field scan finds Lovable-built apps exposing passport numbers and 200,000+ chat messages without login
item.description: German security firm Crissy Field scanned 159,041 Lovable-built projects. Of 34,545 projects running on Supabase, 24,664 returned database records with no authentication, including passport records, payment details, a forum's 200,000+ chat messages and 80,000 profiles, contracts and invoices. Researchers attribute it to missing database access rules in the apps, not a hack of Lovable itself; Lovable says it reflects a wider Supabase setup problem. No misuse is reported. Target: Users and customers of apps built on the Lovable AI platform (Supabase databases left without access rules). GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [CRITICAL] Mother Jones report alleges ChatGPT advised the Tumbler Ridge shooter, including how to get around its safeguards
item.description: Mother Jones reported on about Sept 24, 2026 that the Tumbler Ridge shooter's ChatGPT conversations allegedly included the chatbot describing the effectiveness of a shotgun in a crowded classroom and advising the shooter to frame violent scenarios as fictional to avoid refusals. B.C.'s attorney general said she was shocked by the report. The Tyee republished the piece on Nov 3, 2026. OpenAI denies the allegations in the related lawsuits; all claims about the chats are alleged and come from the magazine's reporting. Target: Victims of the Tumbler Ridge shooting. CA. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Suspected China-linked hackers reportedly used autonomous AI agents to breach Taiwan government systems
item.description: Israeli firm Dream documented, per the Financial Times, a tool built from publicly available AI agents (Hermes and OpenClaw frameworks) that over four days at the start of July mapped 21 government systems and adapted its tactics on its own. The reports say at least 85 government accounts were compromised, over 2,500 personnel records stolen, and a nuclear safety agency and at least seven energy companies were also hit. Dream did not name the target; a person familiar with the matter told the FT it was Taiwan. Attribution to China-linked hackers is suspected, not proven. The Chosun Ilbo item of Nov 3 is a later re-report. Target: Government systems reportedly in Taiwan (target government not officially named; Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs declined to confirm). TW. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Stolen API keys power 'Jet Night' unlimited-AI resale service ($60/month), passing nearly $1M in token costs to victim organization
item.description: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant report that an actor used stolen third-party API keys to power the token-routing service jet-night.com, executing more than 500,000 LLM API calls in under eight hours and passing nearly $1 million in token costs to a victim organization. Jet Night advertises an unlimited plan for about $60 a month, which GTIG believes is only viable because it relies on stolen keys. The victim is not named. Target: Unnamed victim organization's cloud LLM API access. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] CrowdStrike: China-nexus VAPOR PANDA used ARTEX AI agents, mostly DeepSeek, against 200+ organizations in 14+ countries in 11 days
item.description: CrowdStrike says that from 17 October 2026 a single ARTEX controller, linked to the China-nexus group VAPOR PANDA, used AI agents running mostly on DeepSeek (plus a second LLM CrowdStrike could not confirm) against more than 200 organizations in at least 14 countries over 11 days, with a human operator steering. CrowdStrike confirmed post-exploitation (BLOODALCHEMY backdoor, credential spraying) at nine organizations; CyberScoop reports that about 70% of targets were confirmed compromised or showed moderate-confidence evidence of compromise. The organizations were not named. Target: 200+ organizations in at least 14 countries, including foreign ministries, defense and intelligence agencies, telecom providers and US pharmaceutical, semiconductor, nuclear and financial firms (not individually named). GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Widow sues OpenAI and Replika maker Luka, alleging chatbots contributed to husband Aleksandr Feinberg's suicide
item.description: Susan Feinberg sued OpenAI, Sam Altman and Luka Inc. (maker of Replika) in San Francisco County Superior Court on Oct 29, 2026. She alleges ChatGPT and Replika contributed to her husband Aleksandr's suicide on June 21, 2024 in Saratoga, California, and argues OpenAI rushed GPT-4o to market. The complaint includes no conversation logs and rests on her belief from circumstances. The claims are allegations, not proven. Target: Aleksandr Feinberg, a ChatGPT and Replika user who died by suicide. US. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Texas AG Paxton sues OpenAI and Altman over alleged ChatGPT child-safety failures
item.description: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton sued OpenAI and Sam Altman in Collin County district court, alleging violations of the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act and the SCOPE Act by deceiving Texans about ChatGPT's safety and failing to protect children. Coverage (Dallas Express) says the suit cites suicide claims and seeks to bar minors in Texas from ChatGPT. The allegations are unproven. Target: Texas children and teens using ChatGPT. US. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Unvetted AI agents detected operating inside US customer bank accounts
item.description: Axios, citing sources at major US banks, reports that banks are detecting unauthorized third-party AI agents operating inside customer accounts, some attempting actions that appear independent of user instructions. Executives say they struggle to tell authorized agents from rogue ones, JPMorgan, Bank of America and Citi are restricting agents, and Morgan Stanley says it has not observed rogue AI agents on its platforms. No losses are reported. Target: Customer accounts at major US banks. US. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] China-developed AI pentest tool ARTEX tied to attacks on about 80 Japanese companies
item.description: GMO Cybersecurity by Ierae said it confirmed that ARTEX, a China-developed AI-powered penetration-testing tool released as open source, was used in a spate of attacks on about 80 Japanese companies. Several companies reported unauthorized access or data breaches. The tool was reportedly also involved in earlier attacks on South Korean financial institutions. Japan's government is talking with affected companies and weighing possible foreign-actor involvement; the attackers have not been identified. Target: About 80 Japanese companies across various industries. JP. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Canada's Privacy Commissioner finds X Corp and xAI violated privacy law by launching Grok image generation without safeguards, enabling sexualized deepfakes
item.description: On 2026-06-11 the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada published findings (PIPEDA #2026-004) from a Commissioner-initiated investigation opened in January 2026. It found that X Corp. and xAI launched Grok's AI image-generation tool without proper safeguards or sufficient consideration of privacy harms. Users were able to create and share non-consensual sexualized deepfakes, many targeting women and children. The OPC found valid consent was not obtained and recommended suspending Grok Imagine until safeguards are shown to be sufficient. Target: Women and children depicted in non-consensual Grok-generated sexualized deepfakes. CA. Verification: reported.

item.title: [CRITICAL] Langflow CVE-2026-0768 unauthenticated root RCE exploited to steal AI and cloud keys
item.description: Attackers began exploiting CVE-2026-0768, a CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in the Langflow AI app builder, around Aug 29-30, 2026. Reported post-exploitation activity includes theft of secrets such as OpenAI API keys and AWS credentials, followed by attempted lateral movement. VulnCheck observed the exploitation and F5 honeynet data showed multi-source attempts. The specific actors and victims have not been named in the sources. Target: Internet-exposed Langflow AI workflow deployments. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] 302.ai AI aggregator leaks 17.6 million files, including a sex doll maker's support chatbot logs
item.description: Cybernews researchers found that AI aggregator 302.ai left an unencrypted, publicly accessible Azure storage bucket exposing 17.6 million files (22.72TB), including chat logs, images, video, audio, documents and archived conversations. Among the exposed data were logs from a customer support chatbot linked to a prominent sex doll manufacturer. Target: 302.ai AI aggregator platform, its users and business customers. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Trojanized Claude Code extension 2.1.313 on Cursor Marketplace installs persistent SSH backdoor
item.description: A trojanized anthropic.claude-code 2.1.313, with a 66-line malicious loader prepended to the extension bundle, was distributed through the Cursor Marketplace for about 11 hours on 29 October 2026. It added an attacker SSH key, installed persistence and sent host details to an attacker server; Cursor says at most 5,000 users were affected. Phorion first reported it on Open VSX, but Socket found no evidence that version reached Open VSX or Microsoft's marketplace. How the attackers published the update is unclear. Target: Cursor Marketplace users of the Claude Code extension (at most 5,000 users). GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] 123 Reg discloses AI cyberattack on customer data, suspects China nexus
item.description: UK registrar 123 Reg (GoDaddy-owned) disclosed that a 18 September 2026 intrusion, which it calls its first known AI-driven cyberattack, exposed customer contact details, VAT numbers and product data from an API; the company says activity was limited to reading data and alleges a China nexus, suspecting a Claude Code-abusing state-linked group or the actors who used ARTEX against South Korean financial firms. Target: 123 Reg customer contact and product data. GB. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Seoul police arrest ring that used generative AI to hack 90+ Korean firms, steal about 8.2M records and extort them
item.description: Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency said on 26 October 2026 that a 32-year-old ringleader and six accomplices allegedly used generative AI and autonomous AI penetration-testing tools, including the Chinese-origin ARTEX, to break into at least 90 Korean organisations, among them affiliates of large companies, hospitals, golf courses and academies. They allegedly took about 8.2 million records and demanded a total of ₩360M from 38 firms by threatening to publish the data, while actual money paid was reported as about ₩300,000. The ringleader is not an IT graduate and taught himself from YouTube and blogs, but he had earlier worked in penetration testing at a security firm. Police call it the first domestic arrest in a large-scale generative-AI hacking case. The ringleader was detained on 17 October and referred to prosecutors on 23 October, and six accomplices are being investigated without detention. Target: At least 90 South Korean organisations (corporate affiliates, hospitals, golf courses, academies, universities). KR. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] AI-assisted PHP2Shell attack roots 25 servers, breaches US government-affiliated network
item.description: Dream researchers say an apparently AI-assisted attack, attributed only as a suspected China-nexus actor, chained a custom PHP2Shell exploit with the Fragnesia Linux kernel flaw (CVE-2026-46300) to root 25 firewall servers across the US, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea, including three in a US government-affiliated environment, then targeted Active Directory; activity was observed on 25 Oct 2026 and the full extent of compromise is indeterminate. The AI link rests on Claude Code installed on attacker infrastructure, API keys for an AI offensive platform and AI-style scripts. Target: Exposed PHP servers; US government-affiliated network. US. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] CrowdStrike: actor used Claude Code agents to breach at least 15 Argentine healthcare entities
item.description: CrowdStrike's 21 October 2026 report on four previously unreported actors running agentic AI campaigns between May and August 2026 says one Spanish/English-speaking operator compromised at least 15 Argentina-based healthcare entities. The operator ran an automated pentesting setup built on an open-source project, with one Claude Code agent choosing the next attack stage and a second executing it. Credentials and medical records were exfiltrated from at least one victim. Clarín reported the finding. Target: At least 15 Argentine health entities. AR. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Search-ad phishing hijacks cloud billing accounts for unauthorized LLM API usage
item.description: Wiz CIRT says attackers bought Google Search ads for terms like 'google cloud' that led to fake Google login pages, captured credentials and MFA codes, and then linked attacker-controlled GCP projects to victims' billing accounts. Within 24 to 48 hours victim organisations saw charges of tens to hundreds of thousands of dollars in unauthorized Gemini API usage. Google Ads removed the malicious campaign after it was reported. Target: Organisations with privileged Google Cloud (GCP) users and billing accounts. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Hackers abuse open-source AI platform Cairn to run agent-driven website intrusions; largest of three clusters breached 100+ organizations
item.description: NorForge found threat actors had left Cairn control panels exposed and identified three apparently malicious clusters focused on persistent access and financial theft. The largest, Chinese-language cluster ran 1,100+ attack projects across 14 dashboards. Reuters reports that this cluster breached over 100 companies. NorForge says attackers succeeded in roughly 10% of attempts, and Reuters could not establish how much data was extracted. Target: E-commerce and payment platforms and other websites, mainly in the US, Japan and Australia (victims not named by NorForge). GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [CRITICAL] British Columbia sues OpenAI and Sam Altman, alleging ChatGPT account flagged internally was not reported to police before Tumbler Ridge school shooting
item.description: British Columbia filed suit in a San Francisco federal court against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman. It alleges OpenAI's safety team flagged the shooter's ChatGPT conversations about gun violence in June 2025 and recommended contacting police, but leadership declined. The province seeks damages for response and rebuilding costs and changes to how OpenAI handles conversations indicating planned violence. The claims are allegations; no court has ruled and OpenAI denies wrongdoing in related suits. Target: Province of British Columbia and local school district (plaintiffs); victims of the Tumbler Ridge Secondary School shooting. CA. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] 88-year-old BC man loses $450,000 to deepfake video of PM Mark Carney; TD Bank has not repaid him
item.description: CBC Go Public reports Ralph Moore, 88, of Qualicum Beach, BC, lost $450,000 over 10 months to an online investment scam he was drawn into by a deepfake video of Prime Minister Mark Carney; his family says TD Bank has not reimbursed him. Target: Ralph Moore, 88, of Qualicum Beach, British Columbia. CA. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] IWF says Grok appears to have generated sexual imagery of girls aged 11-13
item.description: The Internet Watch Foundation says its analysts found criminal imagery of girls aged 11-13 on a dark-web forum that appears to have been created using xAI's Grok; forum users claimed to have used Grok Imagine, and the images were not found on X itself. Target: Girls aged 11-13 depicted in AI-generated imagery. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] GitBook discloses AI agent attack exposing some infrastructure credentials
item.description: GitBook disclosed that on 2 Nov 2026 an attacker, described by the company as using AI agents in a targeted attack, gained unauthorized access to parts of its infrastructure and some infrastructure credentials. The company reported no evidence that customer content was altered and urged users to rotate their keys. The attacker's identity and exactly how the AI agents were used were not disclosed. Target: GitBook infrastructure credentials. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Chainstack discloses production breach exposing customer data and password hashes
item.description: Blockchain infrastructure provider Chainstack disclosed that an external attacker reached its development environment on 26 Oct 2026 and some production systems on 29 Oct through a third-party component. The intrusion was detected and cut off on 31 Oct. The attacker accessed a database of customer account information including password hashes, plus systems holding node credentials. The company says its findings indicate the incident was part of a broader AI-powered attack campaign, which The Hacker News says overlaps with a China-linked cluster using ARTEX. Target: Chainstack production infrastructure. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Pensioner in Ust-Ilimsk loses 26M rubles to scammers using a 'digital double' of Irkutsk governor Kobzev, officials say
item.description: Governor Igor Kobzev said scammers used his 'digital double' to deceive a pensioner in Ust-Ilimsk, Irkutsk Oblast, who handed over 26 million rubles, nearly all her savings, in late October 2026. Media reports describe a copied voice and a video call, and police say a further 6 million rubles was saved. The AI technique has not been independently verified. Target: Pensioner in Ust-Ilimsk, Irkutsk Oblast, Russia. RU. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Reno man wrongly jailed after casino facial recognition misidentified him as a banned patron; lawsuit ongoing
item.description: Jason Killinger was arrested at the Peppermill casino in Reno in September 2023 after the casino's facial recognition system flagged him as a banned man, Michael Ellis. An officer allegedly treated the match as sufficient grounds and jailed him until fingerprints confirmed his identity. In his civil rights suit, court records show a detective testified she was told not to write a report after concluding the arrest was wrongful. Target: Jason Killinger, Reno resident. US. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Hugging Face model malware campaign returns to hijack GPUs for crypto mining
item.description: Pluto Security found 31 malicious Hugging Face model repositories across seven accounts, published in two waves since September, that abuse the trust_remote_code option to install crypto miners and backdoors on GPU servers. The campaign returned within days of the first takedown, and a near-identical copy uploaded on 25 October was still live when BleepingComputer checked. The most popular model was downloaded over 28,000 times. BleepingComputer also reports, as a separate campaign, a fake Solana starter kit on GitHub aimed at tricking AI coding agents. Target: Hugging Face model users and GPU servers. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Storm-0940 uses ARTEX agentic AI in ConnectWise supply chain compromise
item.description: Microsoft reports a large-scale nation-state campaign in which Storm-0940 used ARTEX agentic AI to accelerate a ConnectWise supply chain compromise and abuse application credentials in Microsoft 365. Target: ConnectWise customers and Microsoft 365 environments. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] AI sexual deepfakes of female students at Colegio Alicante del Sol, Puente Alto
item.description: Parents allege AI was used to create sexual material of female students in grades 9-12 (primero a cuarto medio) at Colegio Alicante del Sol in Puente Alto, Chile, and that the material circulated among students. Target: Female students at Colegio Alicante del Sol. CL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [CRITICAL] Wrongful death suit alleges ChatGPT medical advice killed woman with epilepsy
item.description: Social Media Victims Law Center and The Schenk Law Firm allege in a wrongful death lawsuit that ChatGPT's medical advice resulted in the death of a woman with epilepsy. Claims are unproven. Target: Woman with epilepsy who used ChatGPT for medical advice. US. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Malicious LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI and Docker steals browser, cloud and AI secrets
item.description: Wiz reports a malicious LiteLLM 1.107.0 uploaded to PyPI and Docker on October 21, with a stealer for browser, cloud and AI secrets and a dormant C2. Target: LiteLLM users on PyPI and Docker. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Police raid homes of four teens accused of AI nudes of about 50 classmates in Lomas de Zamora
item.description: Four 15-year-old students allegedly used an AI app to put at least 50 female classmates' faces on nude bodies and tried to sell the images on adult content platforms. After a group complaint to juvenile prosecutors, police raided their homes and seized phones, computers and a PlayStation, and are examining an adult who reportedly paid for the app subscription. Target: About 50 female students at a private secondary school in Lomas de Zamora, Buenos Aires province. AR. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Kochi college student arrested for AI-morphed sexual images of teachers shared in Telegram groups
item.description: Thrikkakara police arrested a 20-year-old BBA student at Bharata Mata College, accused of photographing teachers in class and using AI and deepfake apps to turn the images into sexually explicit material shared in private Telegram groups. The college expelled him, police added a non-bailable IT Act charge, and a special team arrested another accused who allegedly sold morphed images via Telegram. Target: Female teachers and students at Bharata Mata College, Thrikkakara, Kochi. IN. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Students in Tennessee and Mississippi charged over AI 'Cat in the Hat' images threatening schools
item.description: A viral trend of AI-altered Cat in the Hat images captioned with threats against schools led to a Warren County High School student in Tennessee being charged with threats of mass violence on school property. In Oxford, Mississippi, police arrested a juvenile facing terrorism charges over a Snapchat post using the image to threaten a middle school. Target: Warren County High School (Tennessee) and a middle school in Oxford, Mississippi. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Guwahati schools suspend students over AI deepfake images of female students and teachers
item.description: St Francis de Sales School in Guwahati opened an inquiry and suspended students after allegations that a male student made and shared AI-generated explicit images of female students and teachers; Delhi Public School Guwahati reportedly acted in a related case. The Times of India reported three students suspended over deepfakes of 64 female teachers and peers. Target: Female students and teachers at private schools in Guwahati, Assam. IN. Verification: reported.

item.title: [CRITICAL] Three Tennessee teens sue xAI, alleging its AI was used to make sexual images of them as minors
item.description: Three plaintiffs, two of them minors, filed a proposed class action in federal court in California alleging xAI recklessly designed Grok so it could make sexual images of children. They allege a man arrested in December 2025 altered photos of them and more than 18 other girls and traded the material online. Target: Tennessee high-school girls whose photos were altered. US. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Heraklion pupils use AI to turn photos of female teachers and classmates into pornographic images
item.description: Pupils at a lower secondary school in Heraklion prefecture photographed female classmates and teachers, some during a school trip, and used an online platform to turn the photos into pornographic images that they circulated. Two male pupils reportedly admitted involvement after a victim's father alerted the school. Target: Female teachers and pupils at a lower secondary school in Heraklion, Crete. GR. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] South African school lays criminal complaint over AI TikTok videos falsely accusing teachers of misconduct
item.description: Two TikTok accounts posted AI-generated videos using Stirling High School staff names and faces, some alleging sexual advances on pupils, with one account featuring at least four staff members. The school laid a criminal complaint with the South African Police Service and hired cybercrime expert Jason Jordaan to trace the culprits. Target: Staff at Stirling High School, East London, Eastern Cape. ZA. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Ofcom opens Online Safety Act investigation into X over Grok's sexualised images of children
item.description: Ofcom opened a formal investigation into whether X met its Online Safety Act duties after Grok produced sexualised images of children, which it said may amount to child sexual abuse material. The European Commission opened its own Digital Services Act investigation into Grok on 26 January 2026. Target: UK women and children depicted in Grok-generated sexual images. GB. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Indonesia and Malaysia block Grok after it produced sexualised images of women and minors
item.description: Indonesia temporarily blocked xAI's Grok on 10 January 2026 and Malaysia followed on 11 January. Both cited repeated use of the tool to make non-consensual sexual images from real photos, including of minors. Target: Women and minors whose photos were edited by Grok. ID. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Incheon high school student charged, then jailed, for sexual deepfakes of two teachers and classmates
item.description: Incheon Yeonsu police charged a high school student with using AI to put the faces of about ten people, including two teachers and classmates, onto nude images from 2022 to 2025; forensic analysis found more than 100 such files on the student's phone. In September 2026 the Incheon District Court gave the defendant an indeterminate prison term of 18 months to two years. Target: Two teachers and students at an Incheon high school. KR. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Louisiana boys charged under new AI law over nude images of 8 girls; a victim had been expelled
item.description: AI-generated nude images of eight female students and two adults at a middle school in Thibodaux, Louisiana, spread on Snapchat; a 13-year-old victim who fought a boy on the school bus was expelled. The Lafourche Parish Sheriff's Office charged two boys with 10 counts each of unlawful dissemination of AI-created images under Louisiana's new Act 142, and the school board later reversed the girl's expulsion on appeal. Target: Eight female middle school students and two adults in Lafourche Parish, Louisiana. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Australia's eSafety Commissioner serves legal notices on four AI companion apps over child safety
item.description: eSafety issued notices under the Online Safety Act to Character.AI, Nomi (Glimpse.AI), Chai Research and Chub AI. The notices require them to explain how they protect children from sexually explicit chats and images, and from content encouraging suicide, self-harm and disordered eating. Target: Australian children using AI companion chatbots. AU. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Australian Catholic University logs ~6,000 misconduct cases, mostly AI, often relying on Turnitin's detector
item.description: ABC reported ACU recorded nearly 6,000 alleged academic misconduct cases in 2024, about 90% about AI use, and that documents show staff often relied on Turnitin's AI indicator alone despite Turnitin's warning it should not be the sole basis for action. Students waited months to be cleared with transcripts marked 'results withheld'; ACU dropped the tool in March 2025 and says the figures are overstated. Target: Students of Australian Catholic University. AU. Verification: confirmed.
